title: Dynamic shard leasing and cold-store fallback for multi-tenant audit pipeline
creator: Anika Patel
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-aware dynamic shard leasing mechanism and a deterministic cold-store fallback path for audit events generated by RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML flows. This ticket covers ingestion gating, shard lease arbitration, cold spill policy, index lifecycle hooks, and cost-quota enforcement for retained audit indices. Motivation: Large enterprise customers running frequent SSO synchronizations and RBAC admin changes generate bursts of high-cardinality audit events (membership changes, role grants, admin actions). Current ingest hotspots cause long tail indexing latency and cost spikes. Approach: 1) Lease-based shard controller: shards are dynamically leased to ingestion workers based on tenant token rate, event-type sensitivity, and warm-hot capacity. Leases are short-lived (30s) with renewals to allow rebalance during bursty loads. 2) Sensitivity-aware routing: events tagged by SSO/SAML attribute mapping and RBAC v2 severity (privileged, admin, user) determine indexing profile (full index vs compact index). 3) Cold-store fallback: when hot shard queue beyond SLO or when tenant is over budget, events are routed to compact append-only cold partitions with compressed blobs + minimal index fields to keep queryability for audit exports. 4) TTL and compaction: retention classes enforce hot -> warm -> cold transitions with automatic compaction of compact indices every 24h and eligibility windows driven by customer SLA and policy. 5) Tenant cost guardrails: per-tenant budget meters throttle non-critical events and emit quota alerts; high-priority/sensitive events always bypass quota per admin policy. Trade-offs considered: - Index granularity vs storage cost: we reduce per-event indexed fields for cold fallback to save cost while preserving compliance-relevant fields (timestamp, tenant, actor, action, object_id, reason). - Query latency: cold spill increases retrieval latency for some historical queries (expected), mitigated by export job or on-demand recall that rehydrates blobs into warm index. - Operational complexity: lease controller increases orchestration surface; mitigated by leveraging existing runtime leader election primitives and adding visibility in Console. Integrations and requirements: - RBAC v2: need event schema changes to include role_version/role_patch_id for deterministic ordering of admin changes. - SSO/SAML: attribute mapping must surface 'sensitivity' (e.g., is_admin_change) from our SSO sync built-in pipeline. - KMS/HSM: cold blobs must be encrypted at rest using customer KMS keys. - Console: expose per-tenant retention class, budget burn rate, and recent shard lease map. Deliverables: - Implementation: lease controller + shard router + compact index format + TTL lifecycle controller. - Docs: Confluence design doc and runbook for cold-store recovery. - Observability: dashboards and alerts for lease churn, cold-spill rate, per-tenant budget breaches. Links: - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Dynamic+Shard+Leasing+Design - RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/314 - Implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/922 - Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/audit/lease-controller
updates: 2025-01-22: Spike completed comparing lease timeouts (15s/30s/60s). 30s chosen as default after evaluating rebalance frequency vs churn and leader thrash.
2025-01-30: Schema change agreed with RBAC team to add role_version and action_sensitive boolean. PM sign-off acquired.
2025-02-04: Prototype router implemented in ingest-worker; initial integration tests show 2.6x reduction in hot-index write QPS during simulated SSO syncs (50k events/min per tenant).
2025-02-12: Security review kickoff meeting scheduled; SSO team to provide sample attribute maps for sensitivity tagging.
2025-02-20: Backpressure policy added: non-privileged events may be downgraded to compact index when tenant burn rate > 85% of monthly budget. Implementation uses token-bucket meter per tenant.
2025-02-28: End-to-end tests flaky on lease renewal race; assigned to Marco Ruiz and Leah Kim to investigate race window and add jitter to renewals.
comments: PM (Ellen Wong): Please ensure the Console exposes an 'audit recall' button for admins to request rehydration of cold blobs for a time-range and tenant.
Security (Ravi Menon): Confirmed KMS integration plan. Need a short threat model doc for potential cold-blob compromise during export/retrieve flows.
Design (Maya Li): Agreed on compact index schema; suggested adding a hashed object_id to support join-like retrievals without full blob indexing.
Eng review (Victor Chen): PR feedback: unify lease renewal backoff with existing autoscaler to avoid duplicate jitter implementations.
acceptance_criteria: Lease controller successfully rebalances under synthetic burst (50k events/min) without >10s additional tail latency to hot index for privileged events.
Cold-store fallback stores compact blobs with required fields and rehydration path that returns events within SLA (max 2min for on-demand recall).
Per-tenant cost meter emits alerts when burn > 80% and throttle/downgrade behavior matches policy for non-sensitive events.
Docs and Console UI: retention/recall controls present in Console; runbook for recovery published.
Security review completed and KMS integration verified in staging.
